pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 04 April 2026, Shift 2; Q55; question ID 695278430; PDF page 21
pyqs.independentSolution: Full neutralisation needs 28.4 mL of 0.1 M NaOH; adding 14.2 mL converts half the acid to acetate. Acid and conjugate-base moles are equal. Under the buffer approximation, pH=pKa+log(1)=4.75.

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 02 April 2026, Shift 2; Q56; question ID 691121206; PDF page 22
pyqs.answer: Initial pH approximately 2.0; pH at half-neutralisation approximately 3.3.
pyqs.independentSolution: Initial HX=20mL*0.2M=4mmol. [H+]=sqrt(Ka*c)=sqrt(5e-4*0.2)=0.01M, pH2.0 using stated small-ionisation approximation. 10mL*0.2M NaOH=2mmol; equal2mmol HA/A-. pH=pKa=3.3. Exact initial quadratic gives2.011, supporting the stated precision.

targetQuestionText: A 20 mL acetic-acid sample needs 28.4 mL of 0.1 M NaOH for complete neutralisation. What is the pH after adding only 14.2 mL of that NaOH, given pKa = 4.75?
verificationNotes: Both question images and keyed options visually inspected. Teach neutralisation stoichiometry before the buffer ratio, explain weak-acid approximation, distinguish equivalence from half-equivalence. No article yet.
